newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Government decides to set up marine police in 1998.

Provincial government officials refuse to attend dinner banquet hosted by the ruling Nationalist Party in protest of National Development Conference's decision to freeze elections at provincial government levels.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - President Lee Teng-hui and Vice President Lien Chan say people are disgusted at organised crime and violence.
Four officials are indicated for corruption.
Liberty Times - Parliament passes anti-gangster law.
Anti-crime meeting comes up with many rules to crack down on crime.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Central Bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong says the bank will maintain short-term interest rates at between 5.00-5.50 percent before the lunar Chinese New Year.
South Korean cars enter Taiwan market.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Foreign funds flood into Taiwan's stock market.
Taiwan plans to hike property tax.
